{{more footnotes needed|date=October 2019}}

In [[mathematics]], the '''Riemann–von Mangoldt formula''', named for [[Bernhard Riemann]] and [[Hans Carl Friedrich von Mangoldt]], describes the distribution of the zeros of the [[Riemann zeta function]].

The formula states that the number ''N''(''T'') of zeros of the zeta function with imaginary part greater than 0 and less than or equal to ''T'' satisfies

:<math>N(T)=\frac{T}{2\pi}\log{\frac{T}{2\pi}}-\frac{T}{2\pi}+O(\log{T}).</math>

The formula was stated by Riemann in his notable paper "[[On the Number of Primes Less Than a Given Magnitude]]" (1859) and was finally proved by Mangoldt in 1905.

Backlund gives an explicit form of the error for all ''T'' &gt; 2:

:<math>\left\vert{ N(T) - \left({\frac{T}{2\pi}\log{\frac{T}{2\pi}}-\frac{T}{2\pi} } - \frac{7}{8}\right)}\right\vert < 0.137 \log T + 0.443  \log\log T + 4.350 . </math>

This result has since been improved upon, including by E. Hasanalizade, Q. Shen, and P-J. Wong:

:<math>\left|N(T)-\left(\frac T{2\pi}\log\frac T{2\pi}-\frac T{2\pi}\right)\right|\leq0.1038\log T+0.2573\log\log T+9.3675</math>

for ''T'' &#x2265; ''e''.{{sfnp|Hasanalizade|Shen|Wong|2022|loc=Corollary 1.2}}

Under the [[Lindelöf hypothesis|Lindelöf]] and [[Riemann hypothesis|Riemann]] hypotheses, the error terms can be improved to <math>o(\log{T})</math> and <math>O(\log{T}/\log{\log{T}})</math> respectively.{{sfnp|Titchmarsh|1986|loc=Theorems 13.6(A) and 14.13}}

A more precise formula is given by Anatolii A. Karatsuba and M. A. Korolev.{{sfnp|Karatsuba & Korolev|2005|loc=Theorem 1}}

Similarly, for any primitive Dirichlet character ''χ'' modulo ''q'', we have

:<math>N(T,\chi)=\frac{T}{\pi}\log{\frac{qT}{2\pi e}}+O(\log{qT}),</math>

where ''N(T,χ)'' denotes the number of zeros of ''L(s,χ)'' with imaginary part between ''-T'' and ''T''.
